'''Kenan Malik''' (born 26 January 1960) is a British writer, lecturer and broadcaster, trained in [[neurobiology]] and the [[history of science]]. As an academic author, his focus is on the [[philosophy of biology]], and contemporary theories of [[multiculturalism]], [[Pluralism (political philosophy)|pluralism]], and [[Race (human categorization)|race]]. These topics are core concerns in ''The Meaning of Race'' (1996), ''Man, Beast and Zombie'' (2000) and ''Strange Fruit: Why Both Sides Are Wrong in the Race Debate'' (2008).

Malik defends the values of the 18th-century [[Age of Enlightenment|Enlightenment]], which he sees as having been distorted and misunderstood in more recent political and scientific thought. He was shortlisted for the [[Orwell Prize]] in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.orwellfoundation.com/shortlists/kenan-malik/|title=Kenan Malik &#124; The Orwell Foundation|first=Eric|last=Blair-Long|website=www.orwellfoundation.com|date=15 October 2010 |access-date=18 March 2021}}</ref><ref name="gale"/>

==Career==
Malik was born in [[Secunderabad]], [[Telangana]], [[India]] and brought up in [[Manchester]], England.<ref>{{Cite web |title=To Fight Racism, the Left Should Revive Its Universalist Tradition {{!}} Interview with Kenan Malik |url=https://jacobin.com/2023/07/kenan-malik-not-so-black-and-white-interview-race-class-identity-politics-universalism |date=25 July 2023 |access-date=2024-02-11 |website=jacobin.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He studied neurobiology at the [[University of Sussex]] and History of Science at [[Imperial College]], [[London]]. In between, he was a research psychologist at the Centre for Research into Perception and Cognition (CRPC) at the University of Sussex.<ref name="gale"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Kenan Malik {{!}} Enemies of Free Speech |url=https://oslofreedomforum.com/speakers/kenan-malik/ |access-date=2024-02-11 |website=Oslo Freedom Forum |language=en-US}}</ref>

He has given lectures or seminars at a number of universities, including [[University of Cambridge]] (Department of Biological Anthropology); [[University of Oxford]] ([[St Antony's College, Oxford|St. Antony's College]], [[Blavatnik School of Government]] and the [[Oxford University Department for Continuing Education|Department for Continuing Education]]); the [[Institute of Historical Research]], London; [[Goldsmiths College, University of London]] (Department of Social Anthropology); [[University of Liverpool]] (Department of Politics); [[Nottingham Trent University]]; [[University of Newcastle upon Tyne|University of Newcastle]] (Department of Social Policy and Sociology); [[University of Oslo]]; and the [[European University Institute]], [[Florence]]. In 2003, he was a visiting fellow at the [[University of Melbourne]]. He is currently Senior Visiting Fellow at the [[University of Surrey]].

As well as being a presenter of ''Analysis'' on [[BBC Radio 4]], he has also presented ''Night Waves'', [[BBC Radio 3|Radio 3]]'s Arts and Ideas magazine. Malik has written and presented a number of TV documentaries, including ''Disunited Kingdom'' (2003), ''Are Muslims Hated?'' (which was shortlisted for the Index on Censorship Freedom of Expression award, in 2005), ''Let 'Em All In'' (2005) and ''Britain's Tribal Tensions'' (2006). ''Strange Fruit'' was longlisted for the Royal Society Science Book Prize in 2009.

He has written for many newspapers and magazines, including ''[[The Guardian]]'', ''[[Financial Times]]'', ''[[The Independent]]'', ''Independent on Sunday'', ''[[The Sunday Times (UK)|Sunday Times]]'', ''[[Sunday Telegraph]]'', ''[[New Statesman]]'', ''[[The New York Times]]'', ''[[Prospect (magazine)|Prospect]]'', ''[[The Times Literary Supplement|TLS]]'', ''[[The Times Higher Education Supplement]]'', ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', ''[[Rising East]]'', ''[[Göteborgs-Posten]]'', ''[[Bergens Tidende]]'' and ''[[Handelsblatt]]''. He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Arts]].

Malik's main areas of academic interest are philosophy of biology and philosophy of mind, scientific method and [[epistemology]], theories of [[human nature]], science policy, [[bioethics]], [[political philosophy]], the history, philosophy and sociology of race, and the history of ideas.

Malik is a Distinguished Supporter of [[Humanists UK]] and a trustee of the free-speech magazine ''[[Index on Censorship]]''.<ref name="gale"/>

==Politics==
[[File:Kenan Malik talks about diversity and identity.webm|thumb|Interview with Kenan Malik from 17 November 2016 in which he speaks about diversity and identity]]
Malik has long campaigned for [[Civil rights|equal rights]], [[freedom of expression]], and a [[secularism|secular society]], and in defence of [[rationalism]] and [[humanism]] in the face of what he has called "a growing culture of irrationalism, [[mysticism]] and [[misanthropy]]".

In the 1980s, he was associated with a number of [[Marxist]] organisations, including the [[Socialist Workers Party (UK)|Socialist Workers Party]] (SWP) and the [[Revolutionary Communist Party (UK, 1978)|Revolutionary Communist Party]] (RCP), and [[Big Flame (political group)|Big Flame]]. 

He was the [[Red Front (UK)|Red Front]] candidate in [[Nottingham East (UK Parliament constituency)|Nottingham East]] in the [[1987 United Kingdom general election|1987 general election]]. He stood as the RCP's candidate in [[Birmingham Selly Oak (UK Parliament constituency)|Birmingham Selly Oak]] in the [[1992 United Kingdom general election|general election in 1992]], coming last out of six candidates with 84 votes (0.15%). He was also involved with anti-racist campaigns, including the [[Anti-Nazi League]] and [[East London Workers Against Racism]]. He helped organise street patrols in East London to protect Asian families against racist attacks and was a leading member of a number of campaigns against deportations and [[police brutality]] including the Newham 7 campaign, the [[Afia Begum|Afia Begum Campaign Against Deportations]], and the [[Colin Roach]] campaign.
 
Malik has written that the turning point in his relationship with the left came with the [[Salman Rushdie]] affair.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kenanmalik.com/essays/bradford_prospect.html |title=Born in Bradford |first=Kenan |last=Malik |date=October 2005 |work=[[Prospect (magazine)|Prospect]] |access-date=27 January 2010 |archive-date=23 March 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100323015322/http://www.kenanmalik.com/essays/bradford_prospect.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Much of his political campaigning over the past decade has been in defence of free speech, secularism and scientific rationalism. Malik was one of the first left-wing critics of multiculturalism, has controversially opposed restrictions on [[hate speech]], supported [[free migration|open door policies on immigration]], opposed the notion of [[animal rights]] in a series of debates with [[Peter Singer]] and [[Richard D. Ryder|Richard Ryder]], and spoken out in defence of [[animal experimentation]].

Malik wrote for the RCP's magazine ''[[Living Marxism]]'', later ''LM''. Although the RCP has since disbanded, Malik has written for later incarnations of ''LM'', and for its online successor, the web magazine ''[[Spiked (magazine)|Spiked]]''.

In a ''[[The Guardian|Guardian]]'' opinion piece published during the 2020 [[United States presidential transition|US presidential transition]], Malik accused president-elect [[Joe Biden]] of grifting from his supporters.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2020/nov/22/joe-biden-begging-bowl-demeans-the-worlds-most-powerful-post |title=Joe Biden's begging bowl demeans the world's most powerful post |first=Kenan |last=Malik |date=November 2020 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=22 November 2020}}</ref>

Malik has written of his perception that use of [[white privilege]] narratives can further entrench white identity by marginalising [[white British]] working classes.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2020/jan/05/bursaries-might-help-but-not-if-they-label-poor-boys-white-working-class |title=Bursaries don't help when it's not their colour that thwarts these boys |first=Kenan |last=Malik|quote=This in turn breeds greater resentment within sections of the working class about their marginalisation and abandonment and entrenches the idea of a “white identity”, further racialising the notion of class.|date=January 5, 2020|newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref>

Malik commented on the controversy surrounding comments by [[Whoopi Goldberg]] in early{{nbhyph}}2022 on the circumstances of [[the Holocaust]] and also notes at length that [[Nazi Germany]], when embedding their distorted ideologies into law, drew on legal concepts from prevailing [[United States]] legislation.<ref name="malik-2022">{{cite news |last1=Malik |first1=Kenan |title=Whoopi Goldberg's Holocaust remarks drew on a misguided idea of racism |date=6 February 2022 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=[[London]] |issn=0261-3077 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2022/feb/06/whoopi-goldberg-holocaust-remarks-were-born-of-ignorance-not-racism |access-date=2022-02-06 }}</ref>

In March 2025, [[Guardian Media Group]] agreed to pay "substantial" damages to [[Douglas Murray (author)|Douglas Murray]] over a column in which Malik had stated that Murray had encouraged the [[2024 United Kingdom riots]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maher |first1=Bron |title=Douglas Murray wins ‘substantial’ damages after ''Observer'' column error |url=https://pressgazette.co.uk/media_law/guardian-observer-douglas-murray-libel-settlement-riots-kenan-malik/ |access-date=19 March 2025 |work=[[Press Gazette]] |date=17 March 2025}}</ref>

==Works==
*''The Meaning of Race: Race, History and Culture in Western Society'' (Palgrave / New York University Press, 1996)
*''Man, Beast and Zombie: What Science Can and Cannot Tell Us About Human Nature'' (Weidenfeld & Nicolson, 2000; Rutgers University Press, 2002)
*''Strange Fruit: Why Both Sides are Wrong in the Race Debate'' (Oneworld, 2008)
*''From Fatwa to Jihad: The Rushdie Affair and Its Legacy'' (Atlantic Books, 2009)
*''Multiculturalism and Its Discontents: Rethinking Diversity After 9/11'' (Seagull Books, 2013)
*''The Quest for a Moral Compass: A Global History of Ethics'' (Atlantic Books, 2014)
*''Not So Black and White: A History of Race from White Supremacy to Identity Politics'' (Hurst, 2023)
